solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Attractive European's main point

parts.note: attractive in the physics sense, drawing iron to itself, is magnetic
a Pole is a European, from Poland; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a charming continental's chief argument is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main point' is read as an argument's crux, but it is a geographical point: either of the places to which a compass needle points.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic pole is a principal location on Earth that compass needles point to, so it is a chief point in a literal sense.

clue.text: Organized search for piece finally began in shed

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for shed

parts.note: a hut is a shed

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of began

explanation.surface: A search for a missing chess piece eventually began in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a portion, but in chess the pieces are called men; 'finally' picks the end of 'began' and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organized search, typically for a fugitive.

clue.text: Current fashion in fuel for vehicle repair shops

indicators.note: in places the fashion word inside the fuel word

parts.note: gas is a fuel, and in America petrol
the current fashion is 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: The latest trend at petrol stations is servicing cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electricity next to 'fuel', but 'Current fashion' together means RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garages are workshops where vehicles are serviced and repaired.

clue.text: Resort next to Rio getting money through threats

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday resort beside Rio de Janeiro runs a protection racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but is re-sort: rearrange NEXT TO RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining money from someone by force or threats.

clue.text: Religious leaders' one master manuscript

definitions.note: the apostrophe stands for 'are': religious leaders are the parts that follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MA is Master of Arts, a degree

explanation.surface: Religious leaders share a single master copy of a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Imams are Muslim religious leaders who lead prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Potential danger of drop after Portsmouth started with Italian

indicators.note: with joins two pieces side by side
after means the drop comes after the other pieces
started takes the start, the first letter, of Portsmouth

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A football club's slump after Portsmouth fielded an Italian looks risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' may tempt as a verb, but it is a noun here; 'started' takes Portsmouth's initial, and 'after' sends the drop to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or trap, a potential problem.

clue.text: Lie about certain time off work

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of lie are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone lies about being sure they took time off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' reads as a falsehood but is just fodder: 'about' scrambles it into LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time when one is not working.

clue.text: Amount of money earned for being included in minor musical composition

indicators.note: being included in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: minor means small
a tune is a musical composition

explanation.surface: Royalties are earned from a short piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being included in' splits the two-word phrase for a minor musical composition; 'earned' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fortune is an ironic idiom for a large sum of money.

clue.text: A couple of reps imprisoned in brand-new tower

indicators.note: being imprisoned in something means being shut inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: in mint condition means brand-new

indicators.note: a couple of reps means just its opening two letters are used

explanation.surface: Two sales representatives are locked up inside a newly built tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reps' suggests salesmen, but 'couple of' only takes its first pair of letters; 'imprisoned in' puts those, with A, inside the word for brand-new.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Succeeds in getting a first in theology — it's an original

indicators.note: the first letter in the word theology is taken
original here means freshly devised, so the letters of 'it's an' are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A top theology student wins through with a piece of original work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges the letters of IT'S AN into TAINS, which follow A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain is to achieve or reach a goal, so attains means succeeds in getting.

clue.text: Gently persuading, gets a new kilt designed

indicators.note: designed means freshly made to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is gently coaxed into getting a newly designed kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges all twelve letters of GETS A NEW KILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-talking is persuading by flattery or coaxing words.

clue.text: Start to relax on living-room chair

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it is placed after it

parts.note: a lounge is a living-room

indicators.note: the start to the word relax is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone begins to unwind in a sitting-room armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' gives R, which 'on' places after LOUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a type of comfortable reclining chair, often used outdoors.

clue.text: Piece of legislation, say, covering Utah

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to state is to say
UT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Utah

explanation.surface: A law, for example, applies across the state of Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb here; 'covering' wraps it round the abbreviation for Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislative body.

clue.text: Lots of bay trees oddly missing

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters missing only the even ones of 'of bay trees' are kept

explanation.surface: A great many bay trees have strangely disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like a quantity, but it means destinies: one's lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's lot is their destiny, so lots in this sense are fates.

clue.text: Broke? That's new in struggling novelist

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for new inside the rearranged letters
struggling suggests something in disarray, so the letters of novelist are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard-up novelist trying to make a living is told they are broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges NOVELIST to ISOLVENT, and 'in' puts N into it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay one's debts, which is what being broke means.

clue.text: Eleven with child? That's not the main point

parts.note: a side is a team, such as a cricket or football eleven
issue means a child or offspring

explanation.surface: A football team with a child: that's a distraction from the real point.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a team of eleven players, such as in cricket or football.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary matter, peripheral to the main point.

clue.text: Held back artist in sophisticated surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings indicates one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: refined means cultured or sophisticated
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword standard for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter kept himself in check while among cultured company.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts; 'surroundings' says the sophisticated word goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain or restrain oneself from acting, so refrained means held back.

clue.text: A chaotic mixture of jazz music found in Portuguese city

indicators.note: found in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: Faro is a city on Portugal's Algarve coast
rag, short for ragtime, is a style of jazz music

explanation.surface: A jumbled mix of jazz is heard in a Portuguese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is short for ragtime, an early jazz style; Faro is on Portugal's Algarve coast. 'found in' puts the music inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch.

clue.text: Primitive type of cash machine swallowed new visa

indicators.note: the cash machine swallows a card, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: ATM is an automated teller machine, a cash machine

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of visa are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A cash machine has eaten a newly issued Visa card.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a card being eaten; 'swallowed' is the container signal, and 'new' scrambles the card's name before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An atavism is a throwback to a primitive ancestral type or trait.

clue.text: A sailor might be confused

definitions.meaning: a sailor out on the ocean is on a voyage, away from land

explanation.definitionFit: Literally out on the ocean, and idiomatically bewildered, as in the phrase 'all at sea'.

clue.text: The last word on it and youth leader's facility

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so the first letter of youth is taken

explanation.surface: The final word on it is that the youth leader's centre is a useful facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful facility or feature of a place.

clue.text: What a painter might do for second drink?

parts.note: to tipple is to drink, and a tipple is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a painter would order for a second round.
explanation.walkthrough: To stipple is to paint with small dots or dabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is a painting technique of applying dots or small strokes.

clue.text: Winning rows on river and rackets

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it comes after it

parts.note: a player who is up is ahead or winning
to row a boat is to oar it, so rows means oars

explanation.surface: A victorious crew rows along the river amid loud cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels, but it is the verb, OARS, which 'on' places after R.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud noisy commotion, so uproars are rackets in the sense of din.

clue.text: Start of summer and spring is fine in America

indicators.note: the start of the word summer is its first letter

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: The beginning of summer and spring are lovely in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a season beside summer; it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is American slang meaning excellent or fine.

clue.text: Officer in kneepads needed to protect this venue

indicators.note: the clue words protect, or enclose, the answer, so it is found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A police officer must wear kneepads at the skating rink for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a policeman's kit; the letters run through offICER IN Kneepads.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice rink is a venue for skating, the place where kneepads would be sensible.

clue.text: Trying to avoid reversing except I have followed

indicators.note: followed means the following piece comes after the first
reversing tells us the word for except is read backwards

parts.note: save means except, as in 'all save one'
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A driver avoids an obstacle by backing up, except someone has followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' is the old sense of save, as in 'all save one'; 'reversing' turns it to EVAS and 'followed' sets the contraction after.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive describes someone dodging questions or danger, that is, trying to avoid.

clue.text: Bridge across child's practice area for driving

indicators.note: the bridge stretches across, so it goes around the other piece

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
a kid is a child; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A bridge over a child's play area doubles as a driving school track.
explanation.walkthrough: A skidpan is a slippery surface where drivers practise controlling skids.
explanation.definitionFit: A skidpan is a slippery track where drivers learn to control a skidding car.

clue.text: Means of preserving freedom — hardly, with no right to be flexible

indicators.note: flexible letters can be bent into a new shape, signalling an anagram
with no means the following letter is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone argues freedom hardly exists if right-thinking people must be pliable.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one R ('with no right') from FREEDOM HARDLY and 'to be flexible' rearranges the twelve letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Formaldehyde is a chemical used in solution to preserve biological specimens.
